items.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: He relied on George Kates, he was the musical director of the television show... I had no problem with him.

ctx.x: He didn’t do any arranging, as a matter of fact his beginning in music was a correspondence course on accordion. And he started out as a chicken farmer back in North Dakota, and he was a failure at that. And so he decided to take a correspondence course in accordion. And he started out in the business that way as a single. And finally he worked his way into operating a full size orchestra. And he was a smart businessman. That was his other big asset, besides having a good ear. But he relied on George Kates, he…
